prompt.context: Our client is a German luxury car maker. They have come to us as they want to grow their business and are looking into selling their cars in Bangladesh. The GDP growth in Bangladesh is 5% per year. Currently, the only luxury car sold in Bangladesh is Mercedes-Benz, and they have been in the market for the past 10 years.
prompt.question: The CEO wants to find out: if the company enters the market, can they break even in three years?

clarifying_info.q: What is the current market size / how many luxury cars are sold in Bangladesh each year?
clarifying_info.a: Mercedes-Benz imported and sold 10,000 cars over the past 10 years. There are 1,000 new luxury vehicle buyers each year. Existing owners replace their car every 10 years.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average selling price of a luxury vehicle in Bangladesh?
What market share would the client expect to capture?
clarifying_info.a: Do not give this right away — ask the candidate to brainstorm how to estimate market share first. If pressed, the client entered Vietnam and other markets similar to Bangladesh and on average gained 30% market share in each.

clarifying_info.q: What does the cost structure look like?
clarifying_info.a: Initial investment: $7M. Variable cost per car: Manufacturing $20K; Transportation = 120% of manufacturing cost; Customs/Taxes = 95% of (manufacturing + transportation); SG&A = 12% of all above costs.

framework: Market: industry overview, market size, growth rate, trends, competitive landscape (Mercedes-Benz strengths/weaknesses, barriers to entry)
Product: how are client cars similar or different from Mercedes-Benz; same branding in Bangladesh?
Customers: brand loyalty, interest in a new brand, features that drive willingness to pay
Financial Analysis — Revenue: price per vehicle, pricing strategy, number of vehicles sold (market share)
Financial Analysis — Costs: variable costs (materials, labor/manufacturing, transportation, customs/taxes), fixed costs (overhead, SG&A, set-up/initial investment)

questions.prompt: Estimate the total annual market size (in revenue) for luxury cars in Bangladesh.
questions.guidance: Candidate must recognize there are two demand sources: 1,000 new buyers per year AND existing owners replacing every 10 years. Mercedes sold 10,000 cars over 10 years → 1,000 existing owners replace every 10 years = 1,000 replacement buyers/year. Total = 1,000 new + 1,000 replacement = 2,000 cars/year. Revenue = 2,000 × $100,000 = $200M/year.

math.setup: New buyers per year + replacement buyers per year = total market; total market × price = revenue
steps: Existing owners = 10,000 cars sold over 10 years = 10,000 owners; replacement cycle = 10 years → 10,000 / 10 = 1,000 replacements/year

questions.prompt: How would you estimate the client's market share? What share would you use for the analysis?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates proactively propose methods: (a) customer survey to understand needs and how well client can meet them vs. Mercedes; (b) benchmark against comparable market entries. Interviewer should push candidate to brainstorm before revealing the 30% benchmark. The client achieved ~30% market share in comparable markets (Vietnam, etc.).

questions.prompt: Calculate the variable cost per car and the profit per car, then determine whether the client can break even in three years.
questions.guidance: Walk through each cost layer sequentially. Final answer: profit/car = $4K; annual profit at 30% share = $2.4M; break-even = ~3 years ($7M / $2.4M).

math.setup: Manufacturing → Transportation (120% of mfg) → Customs/Taxes (95% of mfg+trans) → SG&A (12% of all above) → total VC; Profit = Price − VC; Annual profit = total cars × market share × profit per car; Break-even = initial investment / annual profit
math.answer: Break-even in approximately 3 years; annual profit $2.4M; profit per car $4K

brainstorming.prompt: Evaluate the potential risks of entering this market.

categories.name: Assumption accuracy
ideas: Market share estimate of 30% may not hold in Bangladesh
New buyer growth and replacement cycle assumptions could be off
Cost estimates (especially customs/taxes) subject to regulatory change

categories.name: Political and economic risk
ideas: Bangladesh political instability could disrupt operations
Currency risk or economic downturn reducing luxury demand
Regulatory changes affecting import tariffs or taxes

categories.name: Competitive response from Mercedes-Benz
ideas: Mercedes-Benz may reduce price; the critical floor is $96K/car (their cost floor) — below that they lose money
Mercedes-Benz could improve service quality if that is the client's differentiating factor
Mercedes-Benz could leverage existing dealership network and brand loyalty

categories.name: New entrants
ideas: Other luxury brands (BMW, Audi) may also enter, fragmenting the market
Market share could be lower than 30% if multiple competitors enter simultaneously

categories.name: Market size risk
ideas: GDP growth of 5% is positive but luxury market could stagnate
Customer base for luxury cars in Bangladesh is inherently small and concentrated

recommendation: Based on the analysis, the client can break even in approximately 3 years at 30% market share, meeting the CEO's criterion — the market entry is financially viable.
Recommend entering the Bangladesh market, subject to risk mitigation measures.
risks: Assumptions (30% market share, cost structure, demand) may prove inaccurate in practice
Political and economic instability in Bangladesh adds operating risk
Mercedes-Benz competitive response (price cut to ~$96K or below) could eliminate the $4K margin entirely
Additional entrants could reduce achievable market share below 30%
next_steps: Conduct price sensitivity analysis to determine optimal pricing strategy and stress-test the $4K margin
Perform competitive response analysis and model Mercedes-Benz price-war scenario
Define market entry mode (JV, greenfield, franchise dealerships, or owned showrooms)
Conduct on-the-ground customer research in Bangladesh to validate demand and brand perception
Assess political/regulatory environment and develop risk mitigation plan
